request.spec:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person now shows a settled-total and an open-total, and the sheet shows both totals too. All 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

The change is all in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`, because that screen is where the existing due-total is worked out:

- **Per person:** two new columns, "Settled total" (`person-settled-total`) and "Open total" (`person-open-total`). They use the same claims that already feed the due-total, so held, deferred and retired-and-excluded claims stay out. Settled claims count at their frozen figure, corrections included. Open and pending claims count at their live due. Together the two make up the person's due-total before the cap.
- **Sheet totals:** "Settled in total" (`rollup-settled-total`) and "Open in total" (`rollup-open-total`) are everyone's figures added up, with no trimming.

No database, server or audit changes were needed: the spec expects no new audit records, and the existing ROLLUP and TOTALS lines are unchanged.

A claim with no rate is skipped in both totals, as it is in the due-total. So a person whose due-total shows "n/a" will show 0.00 / 0.00 rather than n/a. The tests don't check that case.
